model_annotation: The bar chart displays the effect sizes of various mBERT and XLM models across different language families and isolated language categories. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by language family, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," quantifies the effect size, ranging from 0 to 30. Each category on the horizontal axis contains a group of bars representing different models, with error bars indicating variability. The legend identifies the models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). The chart shows that the IE-Indic family has the highest effect sizes, particularly for mBERT-R₂ and XLM-B₂, which exceed 20. In contrast, the Uralic family shows the lowest effect sizes, with all models having values close to zero. The Isolate category also shows low effect sizes, with most models having values near zero. The IE-Germanic family shows moderate effect sizes, with XLM-L₂ and XLM-B₂ having the highest values in this category. The IE-Romance family shows a moderate effect size for mBERT-B₂, while the IE-Slavic family shows a moderate effect size for XLM-B₂. The IE-other family shows a moderate effect size for mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂. The Semitic family shows a moderate effect size for XLM-L₂ and XLM-B₂, with mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ having low effect sizes. The chart indicates that the effect sizes vary significantly across different language families and models, with some models showing higher effect sizes in certain families compared to others.
